What if the cheapest path to $30 million in ARR isn't more users, but fewer payers willing to pay far more? In this episode, Josh from Blue Throne pulls back the curtain on the six-rule playbook his firm uses to buy consumer apps for seven, eight, and nine figures, drawing on six years and some of the biggest mobile acquisitions in the industry. We dismantle the pricing psychology reset ChatGPT triggered, the category-narrowing move that made Flo the first women's health unicorn, and the exit-timing mistake that cost MyFitnessPal over $100 million on its second sale.

You'll unlock the exact valuation math behind growth-story multiples versus last-twelve-months pricing, the cohort-retention signal that separates a sticky nine-figure asset from a UA treadmill, and the premium payer economics that let a 25K-download meditation app clear a million a month. Josh maps the four buyer types who actually acquire apps, the specific metric narrative each one wants to see, and how to construct the deal relationship 6 to 12 months before you ever sit down to sell. Every rule is a cog in one machine built to move your exit multiple as high as it will go.
